question.value: Where does the CO–7.7μm PAH relation break down, and do suppressed PAH emission or enhanced CO emissivity explain the outliers?

evidence.quote: We then assess the local environment, galactic dynamics, and excitation conditions of these outliers to isolate the physical processes that drive these deviations from the global correlation.
We explore two scenarios to explain the elevated CO-to-PAH ratios, which can either be due to suppressed PAH emission or enhanced CO emissivity.

method.value: Apply PAH-brightness and S/N cuts, select ICO/ICO^7.7μm > 10, group adjacent beams and calculate inverse-variance-weighted regional residuals and uncertainties

evidence.quote: To remain consistent with (cite: chown24), we limit the analysis to beam samples with $I_{\mathrm{7.7\mu m}}>0.5\,\mathrm{MJy/sr}$.
To avoid noise contamination and isolate significant outliers, we additionally require $S/N>3$ in both $I_{\mathrm{CO}}$ and $I_{\mathrm{7.7\mu m}}$.

We then identify beam samples with $I_{\mathrm{CO}}/I_{\mathrm{CO}}^{\mathrm{7.7\mu m}}>10$ and group adjacent beams into a contiguous region and compute inverse–variance–weighted statistics to calculate average residual and its uncertainty ($\bar{\Delta}$ and $\sigma_{\bar{\Delta}}$).

key_parameters.value: I7.7μm > 0.5 MJy/sr; S/N > 3 in CO and 7.7μm

evidence.quote: To remain consistent with (cite: chown24), we limit the analysis to beam samples with $I_{\mathrm{7.7\mu m}}>0.5\,\mathrm{MJy/sr}$.
To avoid noise contamination and isolate significant outliers, we additionally require $S/N>3$ in both $I_{\mathrm{CO}}$ and $I_{\mathrm{7.7\mu m}}$.
We define a contiguous region as having abnormally high CO-to-PAH ratio if it satisfies the conservative detection threshold of $\bar{\Delta}/\sigma_{\bar{\Delta}}\ge10$.

validation.value: Test regional significance ≥5 and flux-ratio cuts >8 to >12; main qualitative conclusions unchanged under flux-ratio changes

evidence.quote: If we relax the threshold to $\bar{\Delta}/\sigma_{\bar{\Delta}}\ge5$, additional outlier regions that are relatively small, composed of two to three CO beams, emerge in NGC 1512, NGC 1672, NGC 2835, NGC 4457, and NGC 4548.
As an additional robustness check, we varied the flux ratio criterion applied to beam samples from $I_{\mathrm{CO}}/I_{\mathrm{CO}}^{\mathrm{7.7\mu m}}>8$ to $>12$.
Nonetheless, the key qualitative trends and our main conclusions remain unchanged.

method.value: Select nearby null-test regions in the same dynamical structure with normal CO/PAH ratios, no obvious recent star formation and, when possible, comparable CO flux

evidence.quote: 1) it lies near the outlier region within the same dynamical structure;
2) it contains only pixels with normal CO-to-PAH ratios ($I_{\mathrm{CO}}/I_{\mathrm{CO}}^{\mathrm{7.7\mu m}}<10$);
The null-test regions therefore remain at similar galactocentric radii, show no obvious signs of recent star formation, and have sufficient CO signal for a meaningful comparison.
